review_note: Align the final deck and notes with the lecture’s shorter explanations. Preserve the open-issues and errata structure, quotations, slide order, timings and assessment rules; flag the remaining repeated closing slides and substantive ethics questions separately.

edits.before: - That's the honest reason, and it's why this week sketches rather than teaches. Say it as a limitation, not as modesty.
edits.after: - State the scope limits before introducing the three issues.
edits.reason: Give a delivery instruction instead of certifying honesty and explaining how modest the course should sound.

edits.before: - This is the slide the course has been building towards: a register, stamped, with the course's own name on it.
edits.after: - Keep the three issue numbers visible as you introduce them.
edits.reason: Use the note for orientation rather than another declaration of culmination.

edits.before: - Until this, OI-1 rested entirely on an inventory of how people say they flirt, in the general population. That was not good enough for an open issue with this much at stake.
edits.after: - Distinguish the intimacy study from the self-reported flirting inventory.
edits.reason: Retain the distinction between sources without narrating the course’s research history or praising the correction.

edits.before: The hardest open issue in the course needs **no vocabulary this course hasn't already built.**
edits.after: Two places to start with OI-1.
edits.reason: Do not declare that two earlier concepts supply everything needed for the open issue.

edits.before: - That is a better argument for how the twelve weeks are arranged than anything I could assert about romance.
edits.reason: The slide already makes the cross-week connections; remove the praise of the course’s structure.

edits.before: - We taught it so they could interoperate. Nothing in the material stops it being used the other way, and saying so is the only honest position available.
edits.after: - Ask how using the same technique to make a sale would change its purpose.
edits.reason: Use the existing sale example to expose the ethical question instead of announcing the only honest teaching position.

edits.before: Route two varies a protocol parameter on people who never agreed to be in a study. That is the design, and it is why the reflection carries 35%.
edits.after: Route two varies a protocol parameter on people who never agreed to be in a study. The reflection carries 35%: account for what you do to them.
edits.reason: Keep the marked requirement and its concrete purpose without a defensive declaration about the design.

edits.before:
- Question 1 is the one they will push against. Garfinkel breached expectancies on purpose and it worked -- and he was studying strangers he would never see again.
- They are varying a parameter on flatmates and tutors. Different consent, different aftermath. "Less eye contact than usual" is ordinary; "none at all" is a breach.
edits.after:
- Garfinkel’s method deliberately breached expectancies. This experiment keeps variations inside ordinary behaviour; students may be working with people they will see again.
- The course’s current rule is: "less eye contact than usual" is ordinary; "none at all" is a breach.
edits.reason: Remove the predicted classroom dispute and unverified description of Garfinkel’s participants; retain and separately flag the existing eye-contact rule.

edits.before: **One minute.** Whose parameter failed a question? Hands up. Failing here costs nothing; failing on Thursday costs a redesign.
edits.after: **One minute.** Whose parameter failed a question? Hands up. Use the failed question to revise it before Thursday.
edits.reason: Match the lecture’s practical next step instead of repeating a polished cost contrast.

edits.before:
The slide before says the account "has drawn published criticism".

That is exactly the sort of thing a specification should not be allowed to say without a number attached.

So: **Moskowitz (2004), Psychological Review 111(3), 808--811.**
edits.after:
Which claim can the existing studies test: that high and low power differ, or how each affects behaviour?

**Moskowitz (2004), Psychological Review 111(3), 808--811.**
edits.reason: Replace a staged correction of the previous slide with the methodological question the cited comment raises.

edits.before: - Catch myself doing it, out loud. A vague gesture at a controversy is the documentation failure this whole course is about.
edits.after: - Keep the comment beside the proposal as you explain what it challenges.
edits.reason: The presenter should explain the criticism rather than perform discovering a lapse written into the deck.

edits.before: - Best-formed known issue on the whole reading list, and the model for the next slide but one.
edits.after: - Use the comment’s format for the errata exercise: claim, evidence limit, test.
edits.reason: Keep the reusable form without ranking the paper against an entire reading list.

edits.before: The register isn't finished and was never meant to be.
edits.reason: The E-6 activity already makes the invitation to add entries explicit.

edits.before: - If they are stuck, send them to the "the course's own observation" line at the foot of each week's research review. Every entry there is a candidate, and they are listed for exactly this.
edits.after: - If they are stuck, send them to the "the course's own observation" line at the foot of each week's research review. Each entry is a candidate.
edits.reason: Keep the useful fallback and cut the claim that the documentation was designed for this exact moment.

edits.before: - The reason to say this in the last week rather than never is that they are about to write a capstone using both.
edits.after: - Ask students to identify where their capstone relies on either model.
edits.reason: Turn commentary on the lecture’s timing into an application of the stated limitation.

edits.before: Every entry point comes with what it can't tell you. That is the format, not a disclaimer.
edits.after: Each reading comes with its limit.
edits.reason: The direct description fits the table without another rhetorical contrast.

edits.before: - If they take one habit out of this course, make it this one: find out what the source cannot tell you before you quote what it can.
edits.after: - Ask what each source does not establish before students use it in a capstone.
edits.reason: Keep the source-use instruction without another final-life-lesson cadence.

edits.before: It would be easier to write, easier to assess, and it is the outcome this course was built to refuse.
edits.after: That is not this course’s outcome.
edits.reason: Keep the refusal without claiming that the alternative would be easier to write or assess.

edits.before: - Say it plainly and once. They will have met the other version -- in a programme, a clinic, a well-meaning relative -- and they should be able to name the difference.
edits.after: - Say it plainly and once. Do not assume everyone in the room has encountered a corrective programme or clinic.
edits.reason: Remove an invented shared personal history and make the presenter’s mixed-classroom obligation explicit.

edits.before: - Walk it and name the artefact each part produced. They have built six or seven documents this semester and mostly have not noticed.
edits.after: - Walk it and name the artefact each part produced.
edits.reason: Keep the recap instruction without a claim about what students have failed to notice.

edits.before: - Then the point: a deliberately mixed room negotiated this, one week at a time, and it lets both halves talk about the same exchange in the same terms. That was the argument, and the glossary is its record.
edits.after: - Point to the glossary. Ask which terms helped partners describe the same exchange and where the terms fell short.
edits.reason: Invite evaluation of the shared vocabulary rather than declaring that the course has proved its argument.

edits.before: - This is the last thing the room hears in a lecture. Don't rush it, and don't add to it.
edits.after: - Pause before moving to the capstone exercise.
edits.reason: The deck still has an exercise and several slides after this; preserve deliberate pacing without announcing a false ending.

edits.before: - They arrive at the clinic with something instead of a blank page. That is the entire purpose of these nine minutes.
edits.after: - Keep the paragraph for Thursday’s clinic.
edits.reason: Give the continuity instruction without explaining the purpose again.

edits.before: Three open issues. Five errata. That is the honest state of a twelve-week specification of something nobody had written down.
edits.after: Three open issues. Five errata.
edits.reason: Let the following comparison carry the final satire without another certification of honesty.
